gloss: actually, in fact, to tell the truth

definitions.gloss: actually, in fact, to tell the truth
definitions.explanation: Used to introduce what is really true, often contrasting with appearances or expectations.

examples.japanese: {本当|ほんとう}は{何|なに}が{食|た}べたい？
examples.english: What do you really want to eat?

examples.japanese: {本当|ほんとう}は{彼|かれ}が{犯人|はんにん}だった。
{本当|ほんとう}は{行|い}きたくなかったけど、{誘|さそ}われたから{行|い}った。
examples.english: To tell the truth, I didn't want to go, but I went because I was invited.

examples.japanese: {本当|ほんとう}は{転職|てんしょく}したいと{思|おも}っているが、なかなか{言|い}い{出|だ}せない。
examples.english: I actually want to change jobs, but I can't bring myself to say it.

examples.japanese: {本当|ほんとう}は{甘|あま}いものが{大好|だいす}きなのに、{健康|けんこう}のために{我慢|がまん}していることを{誰|だれ}にも{言|い}っていない。
examples.english: I haven't told anyone that I actually love sweets but am holding back for the sake of my health.

notes:
{本当|ほんとう}は is used to express what is actually true, often revealing something hidden or contrasting with what was previously said or believed.

POSITION:
- Usually at the beginning of a clause or sentence
- Sets up a contrast with apparent reality

USAGE PATTERNS:
- {本当|ほんとう}は〜たい/たくない (really want to/don't want to)
- {本当|ほんとう}は〜だ (actually is ~)
- {本当|ほんとう}は〜けど (actually ~, but...)

NUANCE:
- Often used to confess true feelings
- Can introduce surprising or contrasting information
- More emphasis than ただ/{実際|じっさい}

SIMILAR EXPRESSIONS:
- {実|じつ}は: actually (similar, slightly more formal)
- {実際|じっさい}は: in reality (more objective)
- {正直|しょうじき}に{言|い}うと: to be honest
